stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A thumbtack pressed onto skin with the same force $F$ acts very differently depending on which end touches the surface. Toggle between point-down and flat-down to watch the pressure $p = F/S$ change. Advance once you've witnessed both orientations.
stages.concept: Pressure is force spread over area: $p = F/S$. Same force $F$, smaller area $S$ → much larger $p$. That's why the sharp end bites and the flat end doesn't.

stages.name: Explore
stages.instruction: Swap between three benches — nail on wood, thumbtack on skin, tank vs car on sand — and try both contact configurations for each. Witness four distinct pressure regimes to advance.
stages.concept: Two rules from $p = F/S$: (1) shrink the area, pressure spikes (nail, tack, cleats); (2) spread the area, pressure drops (flat side, tank tread, snowshoes). The force didn't change — only how it's distributed.

stages.name: Predict
stages.instruction: The pressure bar is hidden. For each pair, pick which side presses harder into its surface. Do the mental math from $F$ and $S$ shown in the HUD before choosing. Answer all cases correctly in one pass; a wrong pick restarts the deck.
stages.concept: Same force, different area → different pressure. Bigger $F$ with the same $S$ also raises $p$. When both change, compute $F/S$ mentally and compare the two ratios.

labels.question: question
labels.tip1: same force — flip the tack to change the contact area
labels.tip2: witness four distinct high/low pressure regimes across the three benches
labels.tip3: compute F ÷ S mentally for each side — bigger ratio wins

1.1: The force applied is the same. What changes is the contact area S.
1.2: Smaller S with the same F gives a bigger F/S — that's why the point bites.
1.3: Toggle from point-down to flat-down and back to see p jump by a large factor.

2.1: Each bench has two contact configurations — try both on all three benches.
2.2: You need four different pressure regimes (high or low) across the six configurations.
2.3: Nail-point + tack-point + tank-tread + car-tire covers all four regimes.

3.1: Write down F and S for each side on paper. Then divide.
3.2: The bigger ratio F/S is the higher pressure — that side penetrates more.
3.3: Same F, smaller S wins. Same S, bigger F wins. When both differ, do the division.
